title: September is Attendance Awareness Month
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Around 

Bogan Around Bogan

September is Attendance Awareness Month! Student attendance is crucial to your student's success here at school.The state of Ohio defines chronic absenteeism as a student being absent for 10% of the year for both unexcused AND excused. In addition, the state looks at hours that a student has missed school- not just days. This mean that tardies in the morning and early dismissals in the afternoon contribute to chronic absenteeism.If your family has a fun trip planned, we absolutely encourage you to go and make those memories!! Please just be mindful of other days that your student is absent.We will send monthly letters home if your child has reached 10% or more absences. This is a way for us to proactively share information with you about your child's attendance.Please know that we are here to help!! Do not hesitate reach out if you have any questions or need assistance!

summary: **September is Attendance Awareness Month** at Talawanda High School. Ohio defines chronic absenteeism as missing 10% or more of the year (both excused and unexcused absences), and this includes hours missed from tardies and early dismissals, not just full days. Families will receive monthly letters if their child reaches 10% or more absences, and the school encourages families to reach out if they need assistance with attendance issues.

title: School Health Guidelines: When to Stay Home
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Nurse's 

Notes Nurse's Notes

summary: Students should **stay home** if they have: fever of 100°F or higher, vomiting or diarrhea within 24 hours, undiagnosed rash with fever, active head lice, sore throat with fever/swollen glands/strep, eye infection with discharge, severe respiratory illness, or feel too sick to participate. Students can **return when**: fever-free for 24 hours without medicine, vomiting resolved overnight and can hold down food, diarrhea improved to no more than 2 accidents per 24 hours, rash cleared by doctor, lice treatment completed, 12-24 hours after antibiotics (for strep/eye infection), or respiratory symptoms improving for 24 hours and fever-free. **Stay healthy** by washing hands, covering coughs, and being kind.

title: School Bus Safety Code of Conduct
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Bus Safety Safety at school is our #1 priority, which includes ensuring safety on the school buses. The following Bus Code of Conduct is outlined in Talawanda's Code of Conduct:First Referral: Student/Principal Conference. Will result in a verbal warning and a conference between the student and building administrator. Documentation of the referral and meeting will be mailed home.Second Referral: Will result in a conference between the student and a building administrator, a phone call to parent, and documentation of student misconduct report mailed home.Third Referral: Will result in a conference with the student, phone conference with parent, and 3-day suspension. The administrator will document and mail home the conference summary.Fourth Referral: Will result in a conference between the student, parent, driver, and administrator with a 5-day bus suspension.Fifth Referral: Will result in a conference between the student, parent, driver, and administrator with a removal from the bus until the end of the semester or for a minimum of 10 days.Please talk with your children about the following safety expectations on the bus:Stay seated: Remain in your seat, facing forward, with your feet on the floor and hands inside the bus.Keep the aisle clear: Backpacks and other belongings should be stored under the seat or on your lap to keep the aisle free of obstacles.Listen to the driver: Follow the driver’s instructions and pay attention to all announcements.Don’t distract the driver: Avoid loud talking, shouting, or playing while the bus is moving to allow the driver to focus.Wait for the driver’s signal before crossing: When getting off, if you need to cross the street, wait for the driver’s signal and always cross in front of the bus, not behind it.Be alert and cautious: Look both ways when crossing and be mindful of cars that may not stop.

summary: Talawanda prioritizes bus safety with a progressive discipline system for misconduct. Violations result in escalating consequences: 1st offense - warning and conference; 2nd - parent call and documentation; 3rd - 3-day suspension; 4th - 5-day bus suspension with parent conference; 5th - removal from bus for semester or minimum 10 days. **Key safety rules**: stay seated facing forward, keep aisle clear, listen to driver, don't distract driver, wait for driver's signal before crossing, and always cross in front of bus while looking both ways.

title: PBIS Cafeteria Expectations Program
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Positive Behavioral Interventions and Supports (PBIS) We are so excited to continue the PBIS work we started last year! This week, we held Welcome Back assemblies with our second-fifth grade students. We have a lot of FUN opportunities planned for students this year:Bogan Brave Tickets: Students can receive tickets from any staff member when they are seen following the expectations throughout the building. The tickets will be turned into the office and Dr. Cannon will randomly draw tickets on Friday. If the student's ticket is drawn, they will come to the office to choose a prize!Bogan Brave Student of the Month: Our PBIS Committee selected character traits that we would like to focus on each month. At the end of each month, students in each class will nominate a classmate who has demonstrated this trait to be the Student of the Month. The Student of the Month will receive a certificate, have their photo taken, and will receive a Good News Call Home from Dr. Cannon.The expectations for the cafeteria, hallways, and restroom are below. It would be extremely helpful if you could also review these expectations at home!

summary:
Talawanda High School continues its **Positive Behavioral Interventions and Supports (PBIS)** program with exciting student recognition opportunities. Students can earn **Bogan Brave Tickets** from staff for following expectations, with weekly Friday prize drawings by Dr. Cannon. Monthly **Student of the Month** awards recognize students demonstrating specific character traits, earning certificates, photos, and Good News Calls home. 

**Cafeteria expectations** include: **Be Kind** (use appropriate language, say please/thank you, welcome everyone, help peers, listen to tablemates), **Be Safe** (enter/exit quietly with walking feet, stay seated, keep hands/feet to self, share food only from share table), and **Be Responsible** (use 3-inch voice, raise hand for help, follow adult directions, use tools appropriately, keep table and floor clean).
